assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential body of evidence and framework for understanding how technology and trade reallocate work, reshape local economies and alter inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson form a coherent core for the task, trade-shock and local-labour-market strands.
assessment.maturity: The effects have been documented across settings and have substantially changed research and policy debate over a long period.
uncertainties: The appropriate balance between technological change and trade-shock contributions within a single prize remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and empirical work on productivity, market access and aggregate trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the heterogeneous-firm framework, with Helpman and Redding important contributors to its theoretical development and applications.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in trade research and has generated a large, durable empirical literature.
uncertainties: Credit for the broad heterogeneous-firm trade agenda extends beyond any three-person selection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction and analysis of long-run income and wealth concentration made distributional measurement central to economic analysis and public understanding.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are foundational to the modern top-income research program, while Zucman is central to its wealth and offshore-finance extension.
assessment.maturity: The work has produced influential data infrastructure, broad international research and enduring questions about institutions and inequality.
uncertainties: Data comparability and interpretation across historical periods and countries remain actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have enabled a major advance in measuring intergenerational mobility and identifying the local conditions associated with opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman constitute a closely connected core of the research program and its data-driven methodology.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated, extended and integrated into research on neighbourhoods, education and inequality.
uncertainties: Measurement of mobility is mature, but causal interpretation of place-based correlates requires continuing caution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of collateral constraints and financial amplification supplied an enduring explanation for how credit conditions can intensify macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are particularly central to collateral-cycle mechanisms, with Gertler a major architect of financial-accelerator macroeconomics.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms became core ingredients of macro-financial analysis, especially following major financial crises.
uncertainties: The candidate combines related but distinct mechanisms, making a precise joint attribution challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research established management practices as measurable determinants of productivity and helped connect firm organisation to aggregate economic performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are the central partnership behind the empirical management agenda, with Sadun a leading contributor to its extension.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated across countries and has had substantial influence on research into firms, technology and development.
uncertainties: Separating causal management effects from selection and complementary institutional factors remains demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation research offered a powerful quantitative lens for explaining productivity gaps and the large international differences in income levels.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central to the benchmark empirical-accounting approach, and Restuccia has made major theoretical and quantitative contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated extensive work on firms, distortions and development and remains highly influential.
uncertainties: The extent to which observed wedges identify policy distortions rather than measurement or model residuals is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work made natural capital, exhaustible resources and biodiversity central objects of rigorous economic analysis, with far-reaching implications for long-run welfare.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are foundational contributors to the economic treatment of natural resources and intergenerational sustainability.
assessment.maturity: The intellectual contribution is longstanding and increasingly salient as environmental accounting and biodiversity policy develop.
uncertainties: The empirical operationalization of inclusive wealth and biodiversity values remains incomplete and contested.
